title: Hybrid quant execution paths: FP8-aware kernels, INT8 dequant+matmul fusion and scheduler refactor
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduces FP8-aware matmul kernels and an INT8 dequant+matmul fusion path; refactors request scheduler to expose adaptive batch windows and preemptive slotting. Expected performance: 1.8-2.6x throughput on mixed-precision workloads and 10-20% tail latency reduction for common chat workloads.
description: Motivation: customers running large conversational workloads push two axes of optimization simultaneously: cheaper quantized kernels (INT8/FP8) and smarter scheduling to preserve latency SLOs when batching. This PR implements a hybrid execution strategy that (1) adds FP8-aware matmul kernels with per-channel scale metadata, (2) implements an INT8 dequant+matmul fusion execution path to avoid intermediate FP buffers when upstream weights are INT8 and downstream ops permit FP accumulation, and (3) refactors the request scheduler to expose an adaptive batch window and preemptive slotting to reduce head-of-line and tail latency during bursty traffic. Summary of changes: new kernel files under serving/runtime/kernels/{fp8_matmul.cc,fp8_matmul.h,quant_fusion.cc}, changes to kernel registry to prefer fused path when data layout and accumulation type are compatible, scheduler refactor in serving/runtime/scheduler/{adaptive_window.rs,slotting.rs} with a conservative default policy that preserves existing latency behavior, KV cache interaction updates in serving/runtime/cache to bypass copy-on-dequant for fused paths, continuous batching adjustments to prefer short windows for chat-like traffic and longer windows for bulk embed workloads, micro-bench harness and bench scripts added to infra/bench/quant_hybrid. Commits (high-level): 1) initial FP8 kernel implementation and microbench harness, 2) INT8 dequant+matmul fusion path and kernel registry integration, 3) scheduler refactor and policy configuration knobs, 4) KV cache bypass and tests, 5) docs + benchmarks + small followups. Files changed (high level): serving/runtime/kernels/* (new kernels and tests), serving/runtime/registry.cc (selection logic), serving/runtime/scheduler/* (refactor and policy), serving/runtime/cache/* (KV cache bypass), infra/bench/* (bench scripts), docs/perf/quant-hybrid.md (guidance and numbers), tests/unit/* (numerics and scheduler unit tests). Benchmarks: end-to-end microbench on a T4/80GB-equivalent collector shows FP8 matmul 1.8-2.1x faster than FP16 baseline for long sequences and 2.3-2.6x for short dense matmuls; INT8 fused path reduced memory pressure and improved throughput by ~1.4x in mixed workloads. Tail latency (p95-p99) improved by 10-20% across our chat-like workload mix when the adaptive batch window is enabled with default conservative params. Cost projection: for a typical chat endpoint these changes reduce per-token GPU cycles by ~18% at our sampled workload, with larger wins for model families that compress well to FP8. Testing and CI: added unit tests for numeric parity (relative error tracking with random seeds), integration tests for fused path selection, and scheduler unit tests with simulated arrival patterns. CI initially showed flakiness on scheduler timing tests due to coarse clocks in the test harness; tests stabilized after tightening timing expectations and adding deterministic seeds. Review conversation highlights: Liam O'Connor: "Numerical stability seems OK on the sampled seeds but please add a stress test with longer sequences and underflow/overflow envelopes." Author (Ava Chen): "Added stress test harness and long-sequence seeds, documented the worst-case relative error and safe fallbacks to FP16 accumulation in the registry when scale overflow is detected." Grace Patel: "Scheduler changes look good; can we make the adaptive window configurable per-route?" Author: "Yes, added per-route knobs with sane defaults and a global override for Dedicated customers." Rohit Mehra: "Bench numbers look promising; please add scripts to reproduce and commit summaries of raw results." Author: "Bench scripts committed to infra/bench with a README pointing to s3 artifact locations; raw CSVs attached to Linear ticket ENG-5821." CI & approvals: initial CI run failed on flaky timing test, second run passed; reviewers Grace and Rohit approved after perf/regression signoff; Liam gave an approve-after-changes tag once stress tests added. Migration and config: new config flags added to runtime config schema: quant.hybrid.enabled, quant.hybrid.strict_scale_check, scheduler.adaptive_window.enabled, scheduler.adaptive_window.max_ms. Default values preserve previous behavior unless quant.hybrid.enabled is set. Backwards compatibility: the fused path is opt-in via registry selection and falls back to legacy dequant path on numeric anomalies; no customer-facing API changes. Documentation: docs/perf/quant-hybrid.md contains recommendations on when to enable FP8/INT8 paths, how to tune scheduler knobs for chat vs embed workloads, and an appendix with reproduced bench numbers and command lines. Follow-ups: 1) larger FP8 coverage for other kernels (conv1d, rnn) tracked in ENG-5830, 2) investigate hardware-specific low-level kernels for A100/A800 in a follow-up PR, 3) expand regression testing to include stochastic load patterns in canary. Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2024-11-21 after approvals and green CI. Artifacts: bench outputs and CSVs uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/bench/pr-31207/.
